5º de Primaria · Inglés

Future with going to

Ficha para imprimir
123456
1

Pregunta de arranquePiensa 30 segundos antes de seguir

Si ya has decidido que este sábado vas a ir a la piscina, ¿cómo lo dices en inglés?

Escribe o di en voz alta tu respuesta. Después .

«This Saturday I'm going to go to the swimming pool.» Con be going to + verbo hablamos de planes que ya hemos decidido. Es como el castellano «voy a…»: I'm going to = «voy a», she's going to = «va a».

2

Aprende9 bloques cortos

Plans for the future

We use be going to + verb to talk about plans and intentions: things we have already decided to do. «I'm going to visit my cousins this weekend.» «We're going to paint the kitchen.» «My sister is going to learn to play the guitar.»

It is very similar to Spanish: «voy a visitar», «vamos a pintar», «va a aprender». En castellano también usamos «ir a» para el futuro, así que es fácil de entender. Lo importante es no olvidar el verbo to be delante.

How to form it

The form has three parts: am / is / are + going to + verb (base form). «I am going to read.» «You are going to win.» «He is going to cook.» «We are going to travel.» «They are going to dance.»

In speaking we use the short forms: I'm, you're, he's, she's, it's, we're, they're going to. The verb after to never changes: «She's going to play» (not «plays» or «played»).

Vídeo: Simple future with be going to · Ellii (formerly ESL Library) (YouTube) · 800 mil visualizaciones

Negatives

For the negative add not after am, is or are: «I'm not going to watch TV tonight.» «She isn't going to come to the party.» «We aren't going to take the bus; we're going to walk.»

Short forms: I'm not, he isn't / he's not, they aren't / they're not. Remember: we don't use don't or doesn't with going to. ✘ «I don't going to…» ✔ «I'm not going to…».

Questions and short answers

For questions we put am / is / are first: «Are you going to play tomorrow?» «Yes, I am.» / «No, I'm not.» «Is it going to rain?» «Yes, it is.» / «No, it isn't.»

With question words: «What are you going to do this summer?» «Where is he going to stay?» «When are they going to arrive?» «Who is going to bring the ball?» These questions are perfect to ask friends about their plans for the weekend or the holidays.

Future time expressions

With going to we often use future time expressions: tonight (esta noche), tomorrow (mañana), tomorrow morning, the day after tomorrow (pasado mañana), this weekend, next week (la semana que viene), next month, next year, in two days (dentro de dos días), soon (pronto).

«Next year I'm going to be in sixth grade.» «I'm going to call you tomorrow.» Ojo: tomorrow es «mañana» (el día siguiente), pero «por la mañana» es in the morning.

Predictions: look at the sky!

We also use going to for predictions when we can see that something is about to happen: there is evidence now. «Look at those black clouds! It's going to rain.» «Be careful! That glass is going to fall.» «Our team is winning 4-0. We're going to win!»

We see the signs, so we are quite sure. En castellano: «¡Cuidado, que se va a caer!». Es exactamente la misma idea.

Going to or present continuous?

Sometimes we use the present continuous for future plans that are fixed, with a time and a place: «I'm meeting Ana at five.» «We're flying to London on Friday» (we've got the tickets).

With going to we focus on the decision or intention: «I'm going to study harder this term.» At your level, going to is the safest choice for plans. In informal speech, native speakers often say «gonna»: «I'm gonna win!» It's OK in songs and chats, but in your writing use going to.

Reading: summer plans

Read Gael's message: «Hi Luca! School finishes in two weeks and I've got big plans. First, my family and I are going to spend July in Cantabria. We're going to stay in a cottage near the sea. My dad is going to teach me to surf! My little brother isn't going to surf; he's going to build sandcastles. In August I'm going to go to a science camp. We're going to make robots. Are you going to come to the village this year? Write soon! Gael.»

Where are they going to stay? What is Gael's dad going to do? What is Gael going to make at the camp?

Let's practise: my plans

Make a plans calendar for next week. Write one plan for each day: «On Monday I'm going to finish my project. On Tuesday I'm going to go to basketball…». Then compare with a partner: «Are you going to do anything on Wednesday?» «What are you going to do at the weekend?»

Second activity: New school year resolutions. Write three things you are going to do and two things you aren't going to do: «I'm going to read more. I'm not going to forget my homework.» Repaso: am/is/are + going to + verbo; negativa con not; pregunta empezando por am/is/are.

Ejemplos resueltos

Ejemplo 1. Write a plan: «we / visit / the zoo / on Sunday»

  1. We → are (we're).
  2. are + going to + visit.

Resultado: We're going to visit the zoo on Sunday.

Ejemplo 2. Make it negative: «He's going to play tennis.»

  1. is + not → isn't.
  2. El resto no cambia.

Resultado: He isn't going to play tennis.

Ejemplo 3. Make a question with what: «They're going to cook pizza.»

  1. What + are + they + going to + cook?

Resultado: What are they going to cook?

Errores típicos

  • Olvidar el verbo to be: «I going to swim» → «I'm going to swim».
  • Cambiar el verbo después de to: «She's going to plays» → «She's going to play».
  • Hacer la negativa con don't: «I don't going to» → «I'm not going to».
  • No invertir en la pregunta: «You are going to come?» → «Are you going to come?».
  • Escribir «gonna» en un texto formal: mejor «going to».

Ejercicios

Hazlos en tu cuaderno y después abre la solución.

  1. Complete: «I ___ going to watch a film tonight.»

    Ver solución
    am ('m).

  2. Complete: «My parents ___ going to buy a new car.»

    Ver solución
    are.

  3. Complete: «It ___ going to snow tomorrow.»

    Ver solución
    is.

  4. Make it negative: «We're going to stay at home.»

    Ver solución
    We aren't going to stay at home.

  5. Make a question: «She's going to sing.»

    Ver solución
    Is she going to sing?

  6. Answer: «Are you going to play football?» (yes)

    Ver solución
    Yes, I am.

  7. Prediction: there are black clouds. Write a sentence.

    Ver solución
    It's going to rain.

  8. Correct: «They going to visits London.»

    Ver solución
    They're going to visit London.

  9. Translate: «La semana que viene vamos a ir al museo.»

    Ver solución
    Next week we're going to go to the museum.

  10. Write three plans for next summer.

    Ver solución
    Model answer: I'm going to swim every day. I'm going to read three books. We're going to visit my aunt.

Para familias

  • El domingo, planificad la semana en inglés: «On Monday I'm going to…».
  • Haced juntos predicciones mirando el cielo o un partido: «It's going to rain», «They're going to win».
  • Repasad juntos las tarjetas del paso 6 dos minutos al día durante una semana.

Para profesores

Saberes: Expresión de planes, intenciones y predicciones; futuro con be going to; expresiones temporales de futuro (Lengua Extranjera) (RD 157/2022, tercer ciclo de Primaria).

  • Calendario de planes de la semana compartido en parejas.
  • Propósitos de curso escritos con going to.
  • Juego de predicciones con imágenes: «What's going to happen?».

Qué vas a aprender

  • Talk about plans and intentions with going to (planes)
  • Form affirmative, negative and question sentences
  • Make predictions from what we can see
  • Use future time expressions: tomorrow, next week, this weekend

Palabras clave

going to · am / is / are going to · isn't going to · Are you going to…? · plan · intention · prediction · tomorrow · next week · this weekend · gonna
